newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says will decide on sugar tender Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says will decide on sugar tender Sunday.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan (TCP) said on Saturday it will make a final decision on Sunday on a tender for 50,000 tonnes of white sugar for delivery up to January 11.
"We have received several attractive bids but some of them are without bid bonds or do not conform to our required standard," acting TCP chairman Iftikhar Ahmed told Reuters.
"We will take a final decision on Sunday," he said, adding that an announcement could be expected after 1000 GMT.
TCP issued a tender on December 7 for the supply of 50,000 tonnes of sugar for shipment by December 31 and received nine bids, including one at $358.50 per tonne c & f.
But on December 14, the TCP scrapped the tender and re-invited bids for the same amount with delivery up to January 11.
The tender was issued because of a shortfall due to the delayed start of the cane crushing season in Pakistan.
